seo.title: Sherman Bytes: a pixel tank game that plays on your page
seo.description: Drive a pixel Sherman across a live webpage: breach button bases, build cover and hold the page. Play free in your browser, then get the code.

sections.heading: Sherman Bytes
sections.body: Deploy an M4-inspired pixel tank onto a live webpage. Breach fortified button bases, build your own cover, and hold the page against escalating squads. It plays right here: no install to play, and Recall gives the page back.

spans.text: Play it here, then make it part of your own project. Visit GitHub for the source code, setup instructions, and integration examples.

image.alt: Sherman Bytes in play on its own DOM VIRUS page: enemy tanks roll out of the button bases while the scoreboard counts wave 1, armor and scrap

items.title: Drive and aim
items.body: WASD or the arrows drive; the mouse aims the turret. Keyboard only, the turret follows the hull. On phones, a joystick drives and a round Fire key shoots.

items.title: Breach the bases
items.body: Buttons are bases that spawn tanks. Click or Space fires. Shoot a base down, then sit on it for 0.7 seconds to capture it.

items.title: Hold what you take
items.body: Captured bases stop spawning, repair your armor while you occupy them, and defend against nearby tanks.

items.title: Build
items.body: B builds cover (2 scrap), T a pillbox (8) and M a mine (3). Aim at clear ground; a blocked job refunds its cost.

items.title: Survive the waves
items.body: Siege waves arrive in squads, with an eight-second build break after each wave you clear. Zero armor ends the run.

items.title: Siege
items.body: The mode on this page: waves of squads, a build break between them, and reinforcements from the viewport edges once you hold every base.

items.title: Conquest
items.body: The original capture-all victory condition. Choose it when you put Sherman Bytes on your own site.

items.title: Letters are cover
items.body: Letters block tanks and shells. Blast gaps into faint binary rubble you can drive across.

items.title: Leave firing lanes
items.body: Your own cover blocks your shots too.

items.title: Spend your scrap
items.body: You start with 16 scrap and earn more from combat, clearing text, captured bases and finished waves.

items.title: Find the next base
items.body: G jumps to a hostile base and P pauses. XP upgrades the cannon at 20 and 60.

items.title: A new scoreboard
items.body: A bar across the top: score, wave, armor (red at 30%), scrap and a cannon bar that fills toward the next tier. Auto fire, Next gate (G) and Restart stay on it.

items.title: GET READY, pause and the end
items.body: A 3, 2, 1 countdown starts each run, and the waves wait for it. Pause offers KEEP FIGHTING or SURRENDER. The end shows score, wave, kills, bases captured and your best on this device.

items.title: No zoom mid-run
items.body: While a run is live, a pinch or a double tap no longer zooms the page out of shape. One finger still drives and taps; the end of the run gives the zoom back.

items.title: Same game
items.body: The rules are unchanged; Sherman Bytes runs on Fizlet 0.20.0.

sections.heading: Built from Sherman Bytes

items.title: DOM Battlefield
items.body: Same tanks, a whole platoon. Plan every route, then command your squad under fire.

items.title: Battlefield Blitz
items.body: Same tanks, every crew for itself. Parachute in, call airstrikes, most kills wins.

sections.headingAccent: The same tanks, two board games.

items.question: Do I need to install anything to play?
items.answer: No. Sherman Bytes plays on this page in your browser. Press Play, and hit Recall when you are done to give the page back.

items.question: Can I play Sherman Bytes on a phone?
items.answer: Yes. A joystick drives, the round Fire key shoots, and the Cover, Pillbox and Mine keys build.

items.question: Can I put Sherman Bytes on my own site?
items.answer: Yes. It is open source (MIT). The GitHub repository has the source code, setup instructions and integration examples.

items.question: What happens to the page when I play?
items.answer: Letters block tanks and shells, and direct hits turn nearby text into faint binary rubble. Recall gives back what the game changed and still owns.
